project.name: LinkCheck
project.one_liner: A command-line tool that scans a folder of Markdown files and reports broken links.

walking_skeleton: a CLI command that reads one Markdown file and prints the URLs it finds
summary: LinkCheck is a CLI for documentation maintainers. It walks a directory of Markdown files, extracts links, checks that each target responds and exits non-zero when any link is broken, so it can run in CI.
product_goal: Fail a docs build reliably when a link is broken, with output a maintainer can act on.

users.needs: run it locally and in CI; get a list of broken links with file and line

functional.text: The tool extracts inline and reference links from all .md files under a directory.
Each http(s) link is requested and reported as ok, redirected or broken.
The process exits with code 1 if any link is broken, otherwise 0.
Links to anchors inside the same repo are verified.

non_functional.text: Checks run concurrently; 500 links finish in under 60 seconds on a normal connection.

stack.choice: npm package with a bin entry

assumptions.text: Whether private or authenticated URLs must be supported

decisions.title: TypeScript on Node 20
decisions.decision: Implement the CLI in TypeScript targeting Node 20.
decisions.consequences: Requires a build step before publishing.

decisions.title: Use the built-in fetch API with a concurrency limit
decisions.context: Avoid heavy HTTP dependencies for a small tool.
decisions.decision: Use global fetch with a small worker pool.

layout: `test/` - vitest suite with fixture Markdown files
conventions: No network calls in unit tests; mock fetch
